subject: Next steps: MedSys private deployment economics & env mapping
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@medsys.com>, Dan O'Neill <dan.oneill@medsys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps: MedSys private deployment economics & env mapping

Thanks again for your time this morning — it was helpful to see the traffic profiles and the three-environment topology you described. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before Marcus and Rishi put together numbers.

Recap (from what we heard)
- Token profile: ~50M total tokens/month initially; burst patterns driven by nightly batch enrichment and daytime interactive traffic. 70% generation, 30% embeddings/rerank.
- Environments: Prod (1 region), Staging (1), Dev (shared) + opportunity for DR in a secondary region later.
- Security/ops: Customer-managed VPC, KMS for keys, SOC2 requested evidence.

Pricing / licensing items we need to confirm from Redwood side
1) Target unit economics: you said headline target was roughly $/1M tokens in the mid/high hundreds — you mentioned $800-$1,000 as a target range. Please confirm the target you prefer.
2) Licensing model: MedSys prefers a single annual platform license (on-prem/VPC) + per-token usage reconciliation. We can propose either (A) reserved GPU capacity + discounted token top-up, or (B) pure perpetual license with per-token add-on. Let us know which structure you prefer.
3) Support tier: Standard vs Premium (Premium includes 24/7 on-call, quarterly on-site reviews, faster SLAs). Which level is required for your procurement?
4) Environment count: final confirmation whether Dev will be shared (currently shared), and whether DR will be scoped now or later. This drives minimum reserved capacity.

Attachments: I attached the token projection file you shared with us and a draft license terms redline — Marcus & Rishi, use these as the baseline for a sizing + price sketch.

Proposed next steps
- Marcus: can you produce a sketch of (i) reserved GPU footprint needed for the 50M token profile with 3 envs, (ii) a pricing example for reserved + token top-up, and (iii) a parallel example for an annual license + per-token add-on. Target: send by EOD Tue (2026-11-09).
- Rishi: please surface a recommended support tier and ballpark cost for Standard vs Premium (annual).
- Sara/Dan: confirm whether DR should be included in initial scope and confirm your target $/1M token number (your earlier comment suggested ~$900/1M).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-07T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: MedSys private deployment economics & env mapping

Thanks, Lauren — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- Target unit econ: yes, $900/1M tokens is our internal target for procurement to land on. We understand there's variance depending on reserved capacity.
- Licensing preference: procurement prefers option A (reserved GPU pools + discounted token top-up) because it simplifies capacity guarantees for our clinical workloads.
- Support tier: we'll need Premium for the first 12 months given SLAs on clinical inference.
- DR: we want DR scoped now (secondary region) and will budget for a smaller hot standby.

We uploaded a revised token projection that includes a 2x burst day in month 3 — added to medsys_token_projection_v1.xlsx as "medsys_token_projection_v1_rev.xlsx".

We look forward to the pricing sketches.

— Sara

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-09T07:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Next steps: MedSys private deployment economics & env mapping

Got it — thanks for the clarity, Sara. High-level sketch (will formalize into a spreadsheet and SOW):

Assumptions from their confirmation
- Baseline traffic: 50M tokens/mo (70% gen, 30% embeddings)
- Peak buffer: 2x burst in month 3 (we'll size for burst headroom with autoscale+reserved baseline)
- Env count: Prod (1 region), Staging (1), Dev (shared), DR (secondary smaller footprint)
- Support: Premium first 12 months

Sizing (very rough)
- Reserved GPU baseline: 2 x A100-equivalent instances for steady-state to meet latency targets for interactive workloads + ability to batch for nightly enrichment.
- DR: 0.5 baseline equivalent in secondary region (hot standby).

Pricing examples (ballpark; formal numbers in spreadsheet):
- Option A (Reserved + token top-up): Annual reserved capacity fee: $120k/year (covers baseline GPUs and management). Token top-up: $900 / 1M tokens for incremental usage beyond baseline (we can tier volume discounts at 200M+). Estimated monthly run-rate on 50M tokens: $45k/mo in token costs if entirely billed at $900/1M; with reserved baseline absorbing some token-equivalent, net client-facing monthly bill ~ $30k-$40k depending on how much baseline covers.
- Option B (Annual license + per-token): Annual platform license (one-time recurring): $250k/year + tokens at $1,050 / 1M (no reserved GPU contract).

Support add-on:
- Premium: +$40k/year (includes 24/7 on-call, quarterly on-site, priority SLAs).

Next step: I'll drop a formal spreadsheet and a short SOW draft to the Drive link and post the HubSpot deal note by EOD. Lauren/Rishi — please validate these quick numbers and I'll finalize.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Quick internal summary / action items before I reply to Sara with the formal quote: 
- Marcus: drop the spreadsheet and SOW draft to the Drive link Marcus mentioned. Make sure we show two scenarios (A vs B) with clear monthly/annual math and a worked example at 50M tokens/month and at 200M tokens/month.
- Rishi: confirm whether Premium (+$40k/yr) should be presented as an optional add-on or as required for MedSys (procurement may push back). Also pull any precedent deals with DR scoping for similar customers.
- Lauren (me): I'll prepare a short cover note with the preferred recommendation (Option A with reserved capacity, Premium for year 1, DR included as hot standby) and propose a draft term sheet for procurement review.

Timeline: aim to have the customer-facing quote and SOW sent by EOD 2026-11-09.

— Lauren
